summary: fix(concur): read press-auth captures keyed on the regional host so _csrf is found; infer policyId over HTTP before the report-creation browser fallback
reason: Dogfooded 2026-10-15. (1) `auth login --chrome` failed with `cookie "_csrf" not found` for a signed-in user holding a good press-auth capture: tryPressAuth queried only the apex key, and press-auth keeps a cookie only when its domain attribute matches the capture key (cookieDomainMatches in cli-printing-press internal/pressauth/chrome.go). Concur sets _csrf host-only on the regional web host, so an apex-keyed capture can never hold it, and a regional-keyed capture was never consulted. The printed remedy (`press-auth login concursolutions.com --login-url <login-url>`) recreated the same apex-keyed capture, and a mise shim whose Go toolchain was no longer active surfaced only as an opaque press-auth crash. (2) `reports create` on a policy-gated tenant went straight to the browser fallback on `policyId is required`; that fallback needs its own logged-in automated browser, so a user with a valid HTTP session was forced through a second, separate login. Every report records the policy it was created under (GET .../reports/{id} -> policyId), so the most recent report is enough to retry over the same HTTP session.

changes.description: New. loadPressAuthCookies() lists press-auth captures (`press-auth list --json`), keeps the apex and every captured subdomain, queries them newest first, and pickCookieHeader() returns the newest header that carries every required cookie -- never a blend of captures, because _csrf is minted per sign-in and would not pair with another capture's JWT. pressAuthLoginCommand() builds the capture command keyed on the regional host (derived with resolveReportsUIHost, never guessed; a placeholder when it cannot be derived). pressAuthShimHint explains a mise shim with no active version.

auth login now calls loadPressAuthCookies instead of a single apex lookup; the missing-cookie error, when the cookies came from press-auth, explains the host-only _csrf scoping and prints the regional-host capture command instead of generic log-in-again advice; the press-auth failure path prints the shim reinstall hint and the regional-host command; --help documents the regional-host capture.

New. inferReportPolicy() lists the user's reports, walks the three newest, and returns the first policyId found; retryReportCreateWithInferredPolicy() re-POSTs the create with that policyId. It never replaces a policyId the caller supplied and returns the original error untouched when inference fails, so the browser fallback still runs. The chosen policy name is printed to stderr.

On `policyId is required`, try the HTTP retry first; the existing browser fallback now runs only if the policy still cannot be resolved. A retry that fails for any other reason is surfaced, not retried through the browser, to avoid a duplicate report after an ambiguous write. Long help updated.
PolicyIdRequiredError_TriggersFallback now expects 3 API calls: the extra one is the policy-inference list GET, which that mock 404s so the browser fallback still has to run.

New. Capture-key selection (apex/regional ordering, lookalike and unrelated domains excluded, unusable list output), header selection, a mock press-auth end to end (regional capture supplies the host-only cookie; regional-only capture; unusable list output; no capture), and login-command derivation.

New. Report-ID ordering and policy parsing, an explicit policyId is never overridden, and an httptest-driven `reports create` that proves the HTTP retry carries the inferred policy and the browser fallback is never invoked.
New "Capturing the session with press-auth" subsection; report-creation fallback section and Unique Features entry describe the HTTP policy inference before the browser fallback.
Same documentation changes as README.md, plus the reports create line in the command reference.

validated_outcome: go build, go vet and go test ./... pass. Live 2026-10-15: `auth login --chrome` succeeded from a regional-host press-auth capture with no manual workaround and `account whoami` returned 200; an apex-only capture now prints the regional-host capture command; a broken mise shim prints the reinstall hint; the Chrome custom-named-profile path (upstream 2026.9.6) was confirmed end to end in an isolated --home. The HTTP policy-inference retry was exercised against httptest fixtures built from real response shapes, not against a live create, to avoid leaving a stray report in a real account.
findings_addressed: press-auth lookups were apex-only, so the host-only _csrf cookie was never found
the printed press-auth remedy recreated the apex-keyed capture; a broken mise shim surfaced as an opaque crash
policyId-required forced a second, separate browser login instead of retrying over the working HTTP session

deferred_to_upstream.feature: press-auth keeps only cookies whose domain attribute matches the capture key, so an apex-keyed capture drops host-only subdomain cookies, and a printed CLI cannot declare which key to capture under.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Cross-CLI Printing Press behavior (cli-printing-press internal/pressauth). This patch works around it CLI-side by reading regional captures and printing the regional-host capture command. Tracked in https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5027.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: press-auth login decides the sign-in is complete by finding a sign-out link in the first tab's light DOM. Concur renders none there, and email-link sign-in completes in a second tab, so the capture window does not finish on its own.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Lives in press-auth, not in any printed CLI; needs a press-auth option such as completing on the presence of a named cookie. Not fixable from this CLI. Tracked in https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5028.
